definitionEn: A test done to discover something or check a scientific idea.
example: The students carried out a simple experiment with water and salt.

definitionEn: A person who studies or works in one of the sciences.
example: The scientist wrote down every result in her notebook carefully.

definitionEn: An instrument that makes very small objects look larger.
example: Under the microscope, the water was full of tiny living creatures.

definitionEn: The force that pulls objects towards the centre of the Earth.
example: Gravity pulls every falling object towards the ground at the same rate.

definitionEn: The smallest unit of an element that can exist alone.
example: Every atom contains a nucleus surrounded by tiny moving electrons.

definitionEn: A group of atoms bonded together to form a chemical substance.
example: A water molecule contains two hydrogen atoms and one oxygen atom.

definitionEn: A substance used in or produced by a chemical process.
example: Scientists added a chemical to the solution to change its colour.

definitionEn: A large round body that orbits a star such as the Sun.
example: Mars is a planet that scientists have studied for many decades.

definitionEn: How hot or cold something is, measured in degrees.
example: The temperature of the liquid rose steadily during the whole experiment.

definitionEn: A form of energy that powers lights, machines and electronic devices.
example: The laboratory depends on electricity to run its computers and freezers.

definitionEn: An object that attracts iron and certain other metals.
example: The child discovered that the magnet could pick up the metal nails.

definitionEn: The smallest basic unit of a living organism.
example: Each cell in the body contains genetic material that controls its function.

definitionEn: Tiny single-celled organisms, some of which cause disease.
example: Some bacteria are harmless, while others can make people seriously ill.

definitionEn: Something new that someone has designed or created for the first time.
example: The telephone was a remarkable invention that changed daily communication forever.

definitionEn: A well-tested explanation of how something in nature works.
example: Einstein's theory of relativity changed how people understood space and time.

definitionEn: A set of chemical symbols or mathematical rules expressing something.
example: The chemical formula for water is H2O, which everyone learns at school.

definitionEn: The outcome or effect of an experiment or action.
example: The results of the experiment showed that plants grow faster in sunlight.

definitionEn: To watch something carefully, often in order to learn from it.
example: Researchers observed the birds for several months to record their behaviour.

definitionEn: To find out the size, amount or quantity of something.
example: The scientist measured the distance the ball travelled after each throw.

definitionEn: A substance made by combining two or more different things.
example: The students stirred the mixture until the powder had completely dissolved.

definitionEn: To organise and carry out a particular activity or investigation.
example: The team will conduct a survey of local households next month.

definitionEn: To examine something in detail in order to understand it.
example: Scientists analysed the soil samples to find out which minerals were missing.

definitionEn: To find or learn about something that was previously unknown.
example: Astronomers discovered a new planet orbiting a distant star last year.

definitionEn: To create something new that did not exist before.
example: Alexander Graham Bell is credited with inventing the first practical telephone.

definitionEn: A pure substance that cannot be broken down into simpler substances.
example: Oxygen is an element that is essential for almost all living things.

definitionEn: A substance formed when two or more elements are chemically combined.
example: Table salt is a compound made from sodium and chlorine atoms.

definitionEn: A chemical change in which substances interact to form new substances.
example: The reaction produced bubbles of gas and a strong smell.

definitionEn: The gradual process by which living things change over many generations.
example: Darwin's theory of evolution explains how species adapt to their environment.

definitionEn: A group of living things that can breed with each other.
example: Scientists have identified more than a thousand new species in the forest.

definitionEn: A community of living things and their physical environment working together.
example: Coral reefs form a delicate ecosystem that supports thousands of marine species.

definitionEn: The state of a species or type of plant or animal no longer existing.
example: Human activity has pushed many animals towards extinction in recent decades.

definitionEn: To suggest an explanation that can then be tested by investigation.
example: The researchers hypothesized that the new drug would reduce inflammation in patients.

definitionEn: Correct and free from error in every detail.
example: The instruments must give accurate readings for the experiment to be valid.

definitionEn: Exact and clearly defined in every detail.
example: The engineers needed precise measurements to build the telescope mirror correctly.

definitionEn: To say what will happen in the future based on evidence.
example: Meteorologists can predict the path of a storm several days in advance.

definitionEn: A statement about what is expected to happen in the future.
example: The model's prediction matched the observed temperature changes very closely.

definitionEn: An observable fact or event in nature or science.
example: Scientists still struggle to explain the phenomenon of ball lightning.

definitionEn: A very small piece of matter, such as an electron or proton.
example: The detector recorded the tiny particle that was created in the collision.

definitionEn: Energy sent out as waves or particles from a source.
example: Doctors use controlled radiation to destroy cancer cells in some patients.

definitionEn: The tools or machines needed for a particular activity or purpose.
example: The laboratory bought new equipment to measure air quality more precisely.

definitionEn: A set of fixed steps followed to carry out a task or test.
example: The standard procedure requires each sample to be labelled before analysis.

definitionEn: The preserved remains or traces of an ancient animal or plant.
example: Palaeontologists found a fossil that showed how the early birds flew.

definitionEn: The complete set of genetic material in an organism.
example: Researchers have sequenced the genome of the rice plant to improve harvests.

definitionEn: A disease caused by harmful micro-organisms entering the body.
example: Doctors prescribed antibiotics to treat the bacterial infection quickly.

definitionEn: A substance given to people to protect them against a particular disease.
example: Scientists developed a vaccine that offers strong protection against the virus.

definitionEn: The way that something works or produces a particular effect.
example: Scientists are still trying to understand the mechanism behind the disease.

definitionEn: A conclusion reached on the basis of evidence and reasoning.
example: The researcher drew an inference from the data that surprised the entire team.

definitionEn: To have a close connection or relationship with something else.
example: Higher rainfall tends to correlate with greater crop yields in this region.

definitionEn: To express or measure something as a precise amount or number.
example: It is difficult to quantify the long-term benefits of clean air.

definitionEn: In a way that is based on observation or experiment rather than theory.
example: The claim has been tested empirically across several independent studies.

definitionEn: To reproduce a study or experiment so the same results are obtained.
example: Other laboratories failed to replicate the original findings under identical conditions.

definitionEn: To prove that a claim or theory is wrong using evidence.
example: The new data refute the earlier assumption that the species was extinct.

definitionEn: To suggest or assume that something is true as a basis for argument.
example: Physicists postulate that dark matter makes up most of the universe's mass.

definitionEn: Showing great attention to every small detail in a task.
example: The technician kept meticulous records of every reading taken during the trial.

definitionEn: Different from what is normal or expected.
example: The sensor recorded an anomalous spike that could not be explained by the equipment.

definitionEn: Not leading to a definite answer or final conclusion.
example: The first round of tests proved inconclusive, so the team repeated the experiment.

definitionEn: A range of colours or wavelengths, or a range of related things.
example: A prism splits white light into a spectrum of visible colours.

definitionEn: A substance that speeds up a chemical reaction without being used up.
example: Platinum acts as a catalyst in many industrial chemical processes today.

definitionEn: A chemical reaction in which a substance combines with oxygen.
example: Rust forms through the slow oxidation of iron in damp air.

definitionEn: A measure of disorder in a system that tends to increase over time.
example: According to the second law, the entropy of an isolated system never decreases.

definitionEn: Relating to the smallest discrete amounts of energy or matter.
example: Quantum effects become noticeable only at the scale of individual atoms.

definitionEn: A subatomic particle with no electric charge, found in the nucleus.
example: The reactor uses neutrons to split heavy atoms and release large amounts of energy.

definitionEn: A form of an element with a different number of neutrons.
example: Carbon dating depends on measuring the amount of a radioactive isotope.

definitionEn: An instrument that makes distant objects appear closer and larger.
example: Astronomers used a powerful telescope to observe the faint distant galaxy.

definitionEn: Capable of working successfully or being put into practice.
example: The team concluded that the new fuel was not commercially viable yet.

definitionEn: Done in a careful, orderly and systematic way.
example: She worked in a methodical manner, recording every step of the process.

definitionEn: Open to more than one interpretation, so unclear in meaning.
example: The ambiguous readings made it impossible to confirm the hypothesis.

definitionEn: To provide evidence that supports a claim or statement.
example: The study failed to substantiate the claim that the supplement improves memory.

definitionEn: To estimate an unknown value by extending known data beyond its range.
example: Researchers extrapolated the trend to predict population levels for the next century.

definitionEn: Involving two or more academic fields working together.
example: The centre supports interdisciplinary projects that combine biology with computing.

definitionEn: Relating to the identification of the cause of a problem or disease.
example: The diagnostic test confirmed the presence of the rare genetic condition.

definitionEn: To increase rapidly in number or spread quickly.
example: Cancer cells can proliferate rapidly when they escape normal growth controls.

definitionEn: A permanent change in the DNA sequence of a gene.
example: A single mutation in the gene was enough to change the protein's shape.

definitionEn: Relating to genes or the inheritance of characteristics.
example: Scientists identified a genetic marker linked to a higher risk of disease.

definitionEn: The production of a compound by combining simpler substances.
example: The chemist achieved the synthesis of a new antibiotic in a single step.

definitionEn: The release of gas, light, heat or other substances into the air.
example: Vehicle emission levels fell sharply after the government introduced stricter standards.

definitionEn: Relating to the relationship between living things and their environment.
example: The dam caused serious ecological damage to the river's fish populations.

definitionEn: The variety of plant and animal life in a particular habitat.
example: Protecting rainforests is essential for preserving global biodiversity and its benefits.

definitionEn: The point at which something begins to have a particular effect.
example: Scientists found that exposure above a certain threshold harms aquatic life.

definitionEn: A substance that makes something impure or unsafe to use.
example: Testing revealed a dangerous contaminant in the groundwater supply of the village.

definitionEn: The process by which plants use sunlight to make food from carbon dioxide and water.
example: Photosynthesis allows plants to convert sunlight into chemical energy efficiently.

definitionEn: A practical method of solving problems that is not guaranteed to be optimal.
example: The researchers used a heuristic approach to shorten the search for solutions.

definitionEn: A statement accepted as true as the basis for further reasoning.
example: Euclid's geometry rests on several axioms that were long accepted without proof.

definitionEn: The branch of philosophy concerned with the nature and limits of knowledge.
example: Her thesis examines epistemology, questioning how scientists justify their most basic beliefs.

definitionEn: The branch of philosophy that studies the nature of being and existence.
example: The ontology of the theory assumes that unobservable entities actually exist.

definitionEn: The view that complex phenomena can be explained by simpler underlying parts.
example: Critics argue that reductionism overlooks the emergent properties of complex systems.

definitionEn: Explaining things in terms of their purpose or end goal.
example: A teleological explanation of evolution is often rejected by biologists today.

definitionEn: Involving a random process that can be analysed statistically.
example: The model uses a stochastic process to simulate unpredictable market fluctuations.

definitionEn: Believing that every event has a cause that fully determines it.
example: A deterministic model always produces the same output for the same input values.

definitionEn: Having the same structure or form, so that one maps exactly onto another.
example: The two networks proved to be isomorphic, sharing identical connection patterns.

definitionEn: A line that a curve approaches more and more closely but never reaches.
example: The graph levels off towards a horizontal asymptote as the value grows.

definitionEn: Weak or slight, and not strongly supported by evidence.
example: The link between the two variables rests on a tenuous and disputed argument.

definitionEn: To confirm or support a statement, theory or finding with additional evidence.
example: Independent measurements corroborated the astronomer's controversial claim about the comet.

definitionEn: Capable of being proved false by an observation or experiment.
example: A scientific hypothesis must be falsifiable, meaning a test could in principle refute it.

definitionEn: Vague, unclear or poorly defined in form or meaning.
example: The committee's nebulous goals made it difficult to measure any progress.

definitionEn: The occurrence of fortunate discoveries by accident.
example: Penicillin was discovered through serendipity when a mould contaminated a dish.

definitionEn: To make something unclear or harder to understand deliberately.
example: Technical jargon can obfuscate the findings for readers outside the field.

definitionEn: Present or found everywhere at the same time.
example: Plastic particles have become ubiquitous in oceans, soil and even drinking water.

definitionEn: Having perpendicular directions, or being statistically independent.
example: The two experimental factors were designed to be orthogonal to avoid interference.

definitionEn: A statement that is true by definition, saying the same thing twice.
example: The statement that every square is a rectangle is a tautology given the definitions.

definitionEn: Stubbornly resistant to control, treatment or change.
example: Some pollutants are recalcitrant and persist in soil for many decades.

definitionEn: To come together and merge into a single mass or group.
example: Small droplets coalesce into larger drops that eventually fall as rain.

definitionEn: To make something clear by explaining it in detail.
example: The new experiments elucidate how the enzyme recognises its specific target molecule.

definitionEn: A proposition that follows directly from one already proven.
example: A natural corollary of the theorem is that the sum of the angles is fixed.

definitionEn: The principle of preferring the simplest explanation that fits the evidence.
example: Scientists favour parsimony, choosing the explanation with the fewest unproven assumptions.

definitionEn: Peculiar to an individual or unusual in its own particular way.
example: Each sample showed an idiosyncratic response that did not match the others.

definitionEn: A division into two contrasting or mutually exclusive parts.
example: The debate rests on a false dichotomy between nature and nurture.

definitionEn: Just coming into existence and beginning to develop.
example: The nascent field of synthetic biology attracted considerable investment this year.

definitionEn: Having a clear insight into complex problems.
example: The perspicacious reviewer spotted the flaw that everyone else had overlooked.

definitionEn: More than is needed, and therefore unnecessary.
example: The editor removed several superfluous paragraphs that repeated earlier arguments.

definitionEn: Happening at the same time as something else, often as a result.
example: Rising temperatures and the concomitant loss of sea ice affect the entire region.

definitionEn: Remaining as a small, apparently functionless trace of an earlier form.
example: Humans retain vestigial structures, such as the appendix, from ancestral species.

definitionEn: Departing from what is usual or normal, often in an undesirable way.
example: The aberrant data point was excluded after the team found a faulty sensor.

definitionEn: Composed of parts that differ in nature, kind or character.
example: The sample proved heterogeneous, with particles of varying size and composition.

definitionEn: Uniform in composition or character throughout.
example: After vigorous stirring, the solution became completely homogeneous in colour and texture.

definitionEn: Representing the perfect or most typical example of something.
example: The experiment is quintessential physics, combining elegant theory with careful measurement.

definitionEn: Apparently or seemingly, though not necessarily in reality.
example: The study was ostensibly about diet, but its real aim was to test genetics.

definitionEn: Essentially different in kind, so they cannot be compared.
example: The researchers combined disparate datasets gathered from three different continents.

definitionEn: Not clearly fixed, defined or known in extent or value.
example: The outcome of the reaction remained indeterminate until the final measurement.

definitionEn: Arising unexpectedly from the interaction of simpler components.
example: Consciousness may be an emergent property of billions of interacting neurons.
